blocks.title: Continuity of Operations and Capacity Planning comparison
Continuity of Operations and Capacity Planning exam shortcuts
items: Critical business functions must continue → CONTINUITY OF OPERATIONS
Focus on maintaining essential services during disruption.
Example: Payroll and customer support remain operational during an outage.
Recovery plan fails because nobody knows the system → PEOPLE CAPACITY
Staffing and expertise are the limiting factor.
Example: Cross-train employees for key recovery roles.
Backup environment cannot handle production load → TECHNOLOGY CAPACITY
Recovery systems need enough compute, bandwidth, and storage.
Example: DR servers are sized for expected peak traffic.
Alternate facility lacks power/cooling → INFRASTRUCTURE CAPACITY
Physical support resources must also be planned.
Example: A recovery site has enough generator capacity and cooling.
blocks.example: Focus on recovery speed, continuity, redundancy, data loss tolerance, and site or power requirements.

questions.q: A company wants essential payroll and customer support functions to continue during a major outage. Which concept is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Continuity of operations focuses on maintaining essential business functions during disruption.

questions.q: A disaster recovery plan cannot be executed because only one employee knows the recovery procedure. Which capacity area is deficient?
questions.explanation: The limiting factor is staffing and expertise.

questions.q: The disaster recovery environment cannot handle production traffic during failover. Which capacity area is deficient?
questions.explanation: Compute, storage, bandwidth, or other technical capacity is insufficient.

questions.q: An alternate facility lacks enough cooling and electrical capacity to support recovery systems. Which capacity area is deficient?
questions.explanation: Facilities, power, and cooling are infrastructure capacity considerations.
